definitions.explanation: An electric railway vehicle that runs on tracks embedded in city streets, sharing the road with other traffic. Several Japanese cities still operate streetcar systems.

examples.japanese: {広島|ひろしま}は{路面電車|ろめんでんしゃ}で{有名|ゆうめい}だ。
examples.english: Hiroshima is famous for its streetcars.

examples.japanese: {路面電車|ろめんでんしゃ}に{乗|の}って{市内|しない}を{観光|かんこう}した。
examples.english: I toured the city by streetcar.

examples.japanese: {環境|かんきょう}にやさしい{交通|こうつう}{手段|しゅだん}として、{路面電車|ろめんでんしゃ}を{復活|ふっかつ}させる{都市|とし}が{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: More cities are reviving streetcars as an environmentally friendly means of transportation.

notes:
Compound of {路面|ろめん} (road surface) + {電車|でんしゃ} (electric train). Often shortened to {路電|ろでん} in casual speech. In some regions, locals simply call it {電車|でんしゃ}.

Japanese cities with active streetcar systems include {広島|ひろしま}, {長崎|ながさき}, {鹿児島|かごしま}, {松山|まつやま}, {函館|はこだて}, {高知|こうち}, and {富山|とやま}. {広島|ひろしま} has the largest network.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {路面電車|ろめんでんしゃ}に{乗|の}る (to ride a streetcar)
- {路面電車|ろめんでんしゃ}の{停留所|ていりゅうじょ} (streetcar stop)
- {路面電車|ろめんでんしゃ}が{走|はし}る (a streetcar runs)

RELATED WORDS:
- {市電|しでん}: municipal streetcar (abbreviated form)
- {電車|でんしゃ}: electric train (general term)
- バス: bus (another common urban transit option)
